ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the line passing through the point $(3,0)$: $y=-x+b$ intersects with the line: $y=ax$ at point $P(n,2)$. What is the solution set of the system of inequalities $0<ax\leq -x+b$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given the line passing through the point $(3,0)$ can be expressed as $y=-x+b$ and intersects with the line $y=ax$ at point $P(n,2)$,\\
$\therefore$ $-3+b=0$,\\
$\therefore$ $b=3$,\\
$\therefore$ $y=-x+3$,\\
$\therefore$ $2=-n+3$,\\
$\therefore$ $n=1$,\\
$\therefore$ $P(1,2)$,\\
From the graph, the solution set of the system of inequalities $0<ax\leq -x+b$ is $0<x\leq 1$.\\
Hence, the answer is $\boxed{0<x\leq 1}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Given the line passing through the point $(3,0)$ can be expressed as $y=-x+b$ and intersects with the line $y=ax$ at point $P(n,2)$,\\ $\therefore$ $-3+b=0$,\\ $\therefore$ $b=3$,\\ $\therefore$ $y=-x+3$,\\ $\therefore$ $2=-n+3$,\\ $\therefore$ $n=1$,\\ $\therefore$ $P(1,2)$,\\ From the graph, the solution set of the system of inequalities $0<ax\leq -x+b$ is $0<x\leq 1$.\\ Hence, the answer is $\boxed{0<x\leq 1}$
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a rectangular coordinate system, and the x-axis and y-axis are marked; a straight line labeled y=ax slopes upward to the right and passes near the origin; another straight line labeled y=-x+b slopes downward to the right. The two straight lines intersect at point P in the first quadrant. Reasoning: The given condition states that the line y=-x+b passes through point (3,0), so 0=-3+b, solving gives b=3, therefore this line is y=-x+3. The intersection point P(n,2) is on y=-x+3, so 2=-n+3, solving gives n=1, namely P=(1,2). Also because P is on y=ax, 2=a·1, solving gives a=2. Substituting a=2 and b=3 into the inequality system 0<ax≤-x+b gives 0<2x≤-x+3. From 0<2x, we get x>0; from 2x≤-x+3, we get 3x≤3, namely x≤1. Combining gives 0<x≤1.
